column1: # comment: Bridge2AI-Voice questionnaire/ and pediatric_questionnaire/ symptom items mapped to HPO phenotypes (PHQ-9, GAD-7, DSM-5, ADHD/ASRS, PTSD, PANAS, custom affect, dyspnea index, Leicester cough, VHI-10, voice perception, pediatric PHQ-A, pediatric voice surveys). Psychosocial-impact, positive-affect, and redundant-facet items are out of scope (see docs/mapping-conventions.md). Every object_id verified against the pinned HPO release with oaklib. Revised after clinical review (2026-08-24) - the absent pole was withdrawn set-wide - a questionnaire's lowest answer ('Not at all') denies the symptom within the instrument's recall window, not the phenotype, and that window does not survive into the output - so there is no predicate_modifier column and the set asserts only presence. Only exactMatch and broadMatch rows may carry a when_value.

column2: Feeling bad about yourself - or that you are a failure or have let yourself or your family down
column8: PHQ-9 item conflates worthlessness and guilt (DSM-5 'feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt'); this row = the worthlessness sense ('feeling bad about yourself / you are a failure'); 'Worthlessness' is an exact synonym of this term

column2: Feeling bad about yourself - or that you are a failure or have let yourself or your family down
column8: PHQ-9 item conflates worthlessness and guilt (DSM-5 'feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt'); this row = the guilt sense ('have let yourself or your family down'); exact synonyms 'Unwarranted self-blame'/'Excessive self-reproach'

column2: How often do you have difficulty keeping your attention when doing boring/repetitive work
column8: ASRS inattention item; representative of the inattention construct (careless/distracted/misplace/etc. redundant); the construct is distractibility during boring/repetitive work, so Short attention span rather than HP:0031987 Diminished ability to concentrate; answer >=3 asserts the phenotype present (ASRS Part A scores the hyperactivity items positive only at 'Often'/'Very Often' (>=3))

column2: How often do you feel overly active and compelled to do things, like driven by a motor
column8: ASRS hyperactivity item; representative of the hyperactivity construct (fidget/restless/remain_seated redundant); answer >=3 asserts the phenotype present (ASRS Part A scores the hyperactivity items positive only at 'Often'/'Very Often' (>=3))

column2: How often do you interrupt others when they are busy
column8: ASRS impulsivity item. Ungated on clinical review (2026-08-24): endorsing this one behaviour, even at 'Often', does not establish Impulsivity - the ASRS scores impulsivity over several items and interrupting has non-impulsive causes

column2: Feeling jumpy or easily startled when you hear an unexpected noise
column8: answer >=2 asserts the phenotype present (0-4 severity scale; >=2 ('Moderately') is the conventional item-level endorsement bar)

column2: Being 'super alert', on guard, or constantly on the lookout for danger
column8: 'super alert, on guard, on the lookout for danger' = hypervigilance; answer >=2 asserts the phenotype present (0-4 severity scale; >=2 ('Moderately') is the conventional item-level endorsement bar)

column2: Being extremely irritable or angry to the point of yelling, fights, or destroying things

column2: Being extremely irritable or angry to the point of yelling, fights, or destroying things
column8: item names three senses; this row = the anger sense - HP:0031473 is directed hostility toward a provocation, distinct from Irritability's lowered reactivity threshold

column2: Being extremely irritable or angry to the point of yelling, fights, or destroying things
column8: item names three senses; this row = the behavioural escalation ('yelling, fights, destroying things'), which HPO's definition names as shouting and harming physical property; not subsumable by HP:0031467, which sits in a different branch (Disinhibition)

column2: Losing interest in activities you used to enjoy before a stressful experience
column8: the item is event-related ('before a stressful experience') while Anhedonia covers event-related and unrelated loss of pleasure alike, so the HPO term is broader (clinical review, 2026-08-24); answer >=2 asserts the phenotype present (0-4 severity scale; >=2 ('Moderately') is the conventional item-level endorsement bar)

column2: Hostile
column8: PANAS momentary-state affect rating; 'Hostile'/'Hostility' are exact synonyms of Anger (previously mapped to HP:0000737 Irritability, where they are not synonyms). Not HP:0000718 Aggressive behavior: the data dict defines this as 'feeling hostile (angry or irritable)', a state, whereas HP:0000718 is an act aimed at harming, under Disinhibition

column2: Feeling down, depressed, or hopeless
column8: 'Feeling down, depressed, or hopeless' is a normal-range mood descriptor, whereas HP:5200273 requires sadness 'excessive in intensity, duration, or resistance to self-regulation'; neither subsumes the other (clinical review, 2026-08-24). Ungated: a relatedMatch cannot support a present assertion

column2: Little interest or pleasure in doing things
column8: answer >=2 asserts the phenotype present (DSM-5 Level 1 treats Mild (2) or greater as the threshold for further inquiry); harmonized with phq9/gad7 on the answer LABEL not the integer: dsm5_adult has an extra rung at the bottom, so its 'Mild (Several days)'=2 is the same severity as phq9's 'Several days'=1

column2: Feeling nervous, anxious, frightened, worried, or on edge
column8: answer >=2 asserts the phenotype present (DSM-5 Level 1 treats Mild (2) or greater as the threshold for further inquiry); harmonized with phq9/gad7 on the answer LABEL not the integer: dsm5_adult has an extra rung at the bottom, so its 'Mild (Several days)'=2 is the same severity as phq9's 'Several days'=1

column2: Feeling panic or being frightened
column8: 'Feeling panic or being frightened' is not a Panic attack, which HPO defines as a discrete episode of intense fear with somatic features (clinical review, 2026-08-24). Ungated: a relatedMatch cannot support a present assertion

column2: Feeling more irritated, grouchy, or angry than usual
column8: item conflates irritation/grouchiness and anger; this row = the irritation sense ('Grumpy'/'Cranky' are exact synonyms of Irritability)

column2: Hearing things other people couldn't hear, such as voices when no one was around
column8: answer >=1 asserts the phenotype present (DSM-5 Level 1 lowers the threshold to Slight (1) for the psychosis domain)

column2: Feeling that someone could hear your thoughts, or that you could hear another person's thoughts
column8: item conflates two thought-alienation phenomena; this row = the outbound sense ('someone could hear your thoughts'), which HPO defines as the belief that everyone knows what you are thinking. Was broadMatch to the parent HP:5200419, whose definition is a delusion of control and describes neither sense

column2: Problems with memory (learning new information) or with location (finding your way home)
column8: item conflates memory and spatial orientation ('finding your way home') in one yes/no answer, so the memory-specific HP:0002354 overstates it; HPO has no topographical/spatial-disorientation term (nearest are Left-right disorientation, Impaired visuospatial constructive cognition, Confusion - none is wayfinding), so a per-sense split would drop the location facet. Cognitive impairment subsumes both and its own definition names 'learning new things'; answer >=2 asserts the phenotype present (DSM-5 Level 1 treats Mild (2) or greater as the threshold for further inquiry)

column2: Unexplained aches and pains (e.g., head, back, joints, abdomen, legs)
column8: unexplained aches/pains at multiple sites; generic Pain subsumes them; answer >=2 asserts the phenotype present (DSM-5 Level 1 treats Mild (2) or greater as the threshold for further inquiry)

column2: Feeling driven to perform certain behaviors or mental acts over and over again

column2: Feeling detached or distant from yourself, your body, surroundings, or memories
